# Write storylines — harden, document, and improve the Main Street storyline system

> **Status: DRAFT — pending producer answers (see Appendix).** This brief was
> drafted from repo research. Three open questions materially change its shape
> and are recorded in the Appendix and on the work item. Do not treat the
> provisional Acceptance Criteria below as final until the questions are
> answered.

## Problem statement

Main Street has a *rough* storyline implementation: incident event cards can
carry a dual choice (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`)
and the player's Accept/Reject decision schedules the next card in a chain
(`CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`). The mechanic works and is tested, but it is thin,
implicit, and undocumented: the branching model supports only binary choices
with one successor per branch, there is no authoring/validation tooling, the
storyline graph is invisible to both developers and players, and there is no
documentation explaining how storylines are created and managed. This makes
storylines hard to extend safely and invisible as a source of player agency.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to author, extend and balance
  storylines (new chains, retro-fitting existing incidents) without editing
  engine code, and to see the shape of a storyline at a glance.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need a documented, validated, and
  flexible data model with clear extension seams and a safety net (static
  validation of chain links) so storyline changes cannot silently break.
- **Players** — should feel that their choices shape an unfolding story, with
  visible continuity (what they chose, what it led to) rather than two opaque
  buttons.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — need a documented decision policy for storyline
  choices that scales as the branching model grows.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to define a storyline declaratively (cards +
  links + choice text) and run a validator, so I know every branch resolves
  before I ship it."
- "As a developer, I want a documented storyline model and an authoring guide,
  so I can add a multi-step chain without reverse-engineering the engine."
- "As a player, I want to see the consequences of my past choices (a storyline
  journal/history), so my decisions feel like they build a narrative."
- "As a producer, I want a concrete, prioritised list of tooling and
  player-agency improvements, so I can schedule the next iteration."

## Acceptance Criteria (provisional — pending Appendix answers)

> AC1, AC6 and AC7 are shape-dependent on the open questions. The list below
> assumes the **recommended** options (epic; propose-and-schedule improvements;
> Main Street-specific hardening).

1. **Documentation exists and is complete** — a single canonical document
   (`docs/main-street/storylines.md`, plus a short `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
   cross-reference) explains: what a storyline is, the data model
   (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`), the resolution
   lifecycle (deferred `pendingEventChoice`, accept/reject paths, deck
   insertion, undo/redo, save/load, transcript), the AI policy, and — most
   importantly — **how to author and manage a storyline end to end**, with a
   worked example and a checklist.
2. **Data model hardened and validated** — every storyline link in
   `card-data.csv` is validated statically (all `acceptNextCardId` /
   `rejectNextCardId` targets resolve to existing cards; no dangling links; no
   self-links unless intended; chains terminate or cycle by design). Validation
   fails the build / a dedicated script rather than only logging at runtime.
3. **Model made more flexible** — the storyline model supports at least one
   documented extension seam beyond strict binary accept/reject (e.g. >2
   options, conditional successors, or per-storyline metadata), or the brief
   explicitly records why the binary model is the deliberate limit.
4. **Improvement proposals captured** — a prioritised, evidence-backed list of
   improvements is produced for (a) **tooling** (authoring, validation,
   visualisation) and (b) **player agency** (visibility, continuity,
   meaningfulness), each as a separate, schedulable work item — not scope
   inside this item.
5. **Documentation is tested** — at least one test or doc-lint check asserts
   that the canonical storyline docs exist and that documented chain examples
   match the shipped CSV (guards against doc/code drift).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility** — existing cards without storyline fields must
  behave exactly as before; old saves must load (missing fields treated as
  non-choice / null).
- **Determinism / replay safety** — storyline resolution must remain
  deterministic (`pushChainCard` must not consume RNG or wall-clock time);
  transcripts must stay replayable.
- **No cheating on cost** — event choices are and remain free (no daily-action
  cost); this is a forced reaction, not a chosen engagement.
- **Existing event-flow decisions preserved** — deferred end-of-turn mutation,
  undo/redo semantics, AI difficulty policy and tutorial exclusion of choice
  events must not regress.
- **No new runtime dependency** for validation tooling beyond the existing
  Node/Vitest/scripts toolchain.

## Existing state (repo research)

### Data model
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` gains
  `hasChoices?: boolean`, `acceptNextCardId?: string | null`,
  `rejectNextCardId?: string | null` (`DurationEventCard` inherits them).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — header already contains the three
  columns. **7 choice cards** currently ship:
  `evt-tax` (→ `evt-tax-inquiry` on reject), `evt-flu-outbreak` (→
  `evt-pandemic`), `evt-recession` (→ `evt-depression`), `evt-tax-error`
  (→ `evt-tax`), `evt-tax-inquiry` (→ `evt-tax-error` on accept, i.e. cycle),
  `evt-strike-service` (→ `evt-general-strike`), `evt-popular-menu`
  (→ `evt-farm-table`).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` parses the three CSV
  columns into the typed fields.

### Engine / lifecycle
- `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveIncident()` intercepts
  `hasChoices`, stashes `state.pendingEventChoice`, returns `null`;
  `resolveEventChoice()` implements accept (apply effect + push
  `acceptNextCardId`) and reject (skip effect + push `rejectNextCardId`);
  `pushChainCard()` builds a fresh instance and pushes it to the **top** of the
  incident deck with a deterministic serial; `processEndOfTurn()` pauses with
  `TurnResult.choicePending`.
- `MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — typed `PendingEventChoice` on `MainStreetState`
  (`{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`).
- `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialises/backfills `pendingEventChoice`.
- `MainStreetCommands.ts` — snapshot-based undo/redo of the choice.
- `MainStreetTranscript.ts` — records `{ type: 'event-choice', eventId,
  cardName, option, acceptNextCardId, rejectNextCardId }`.

### UI
- `scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showEventChoiceDialog(event,
  onAccept, onReject)` (Accept/Reject buttons, no preview of the escalation,
  overlay depth conventions).
- `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — shows the dialog when
  `choicePending` is observed; reduced-motion aware.

### AI
- `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice(state, event, difficulty)`
  (Easy: always accept; Medium: accept if manageable; Hard: static full-chain
  severity comparison + `AI_EVENT_CHOICE_SIGNIFICANTLY_WORSE_RATIO`).
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `resolveAiEventChoice()` resolves pending choices
  in headless/AI turns.

### Tests
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts`, `event-choice*.test.ts`,
  `MainStreetEventChoice*.test.ts`, `MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts`,
  `ai-choice.test.ts`, `tutorial-choice-exclusion.test.ts`,
  `event-choice-dialog*.browser.test.ts`, `incident-*.test.ts`.

### Gaps observed
- **No documentation** of the storyline model or authoring process anywhere in
  `docs/` (only a passing mention of "event choices" in
  `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`).
- **No static validation tooling** — a dangling `acceptNextCardId` is only
  logged at runtime (`Chain card X not found in card data.`).
- **No authoring/visualisation tooling** — no schema, generator, or graph view;
  chains are edited by hand in a 155-row CSV.
- **Binary-only branching** — one accept and one reject successor; no
  multi-option, conditional, weighted, or state-gated successor.
- **No storyline identity/history** — chains are anonymous card links; there is
  no storyline id/name/chapter, no memory of past choices, and no player-facing
  journal.
- **Content child still open** — `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` ("Content: New chain
  cards and retro-fitting") is `status=open`, `stage=plan_complete`, despite
  the chain content appearing to ship; reconcile this.
- **No toggles** — storylines cannot be enabled/disabled per difficulty or
  tutorial beyond the tutorial excluding choice events entirely.

## Desired change

1. **Harden** the existing model: add static chain validation; reconcile the
   open content child; close documentation/code-comment gaps; ensure the model
   is explicitly documented as the contract.
2. **Make it more detailed and flexible**: decide and document the branching
   contract (binary vs extensible), and add the minimal, well-tested extension
   seam that supports future storylines without over-engineering.
3. **Document** the full lifecycle end to end for content designers and
   developers.
4. **Propose** prioritised tooling and player-agency improvements as separate
   work items.
5. **Test** the hardened model and guard against doc/code drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — **new** canonical documentation: model,
  lifecycle, authoring guide, worked example, checklist.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — cross-reference / short summary section.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — CSV column reference for storyline
  columns and link to the new doc.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — chain data (validation target,
  possible extension fields).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — documented model /
  possible extension fields.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — CSV parsing for new
  columns.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution,
  `pushChainCard`, validation hooks.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingEventChoice`
  shape if extended.
- `scripts/` (e.g. `scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) — **new** static
  validation entry point.
- `tests/main-street/` — validation + model + doc-drift tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-engineering risk** — expanding the branching model prematurely could
  destabilise a shipped mechanic. *Mitigation:* prefer a documented seam over a
  large rewrite; gate on the producer's answer to Q2/Q3.
- **Scope-creep risk** — "improvements for tooling and player agency" could
  balloon. *Mitigation:* capture as separate work items (AC4), not scope.
- **Doc/code drift** — documentation can rot. *Mitigation:* doc-drift test
  (AC5).
- **Content/engine coupling** — chain links live in a hand-edited CSV;
  validation must fail loudly. *Mitigation:* AC2.
- **Assumption** — "storylines" means the Main Street incident event-chain
  system (`hasChoices` model) built by `CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`; there is no other
  storyline implementation in the repo.
- **Assumption** — documentation audience is primarily developers + content
  designers; player-facing narrative text is content work, not this doc.
- **Assumption** — this work does not require schema/release-pipeline changes;
  CHANGELOG is managed by the ship/release pipeline.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128** — "Story-driven event chains with dual-choice
  consequences" (completed, shipped v0.1.16) — the parent implementation this
  item hardens and documents. Children: `CG-0MTT7DUJE002HPPM` (data model),
  `CG-0MTT7E4FX007QCUR` (engine), `CG-0MTT7EFYH006N940` (UI),
  `CG-0MTT7EQZP005NWGQ` (AI), `CG-0MTT7F1JG007E7UL` (persistence/undo),
  `CG-0MTT7FO7I009295E` (tutorial exclusion), `CG-0MTT78RRQ0056KUZ` /
  `CG-0MTT7DB850037SMW` / `CG-0MTT7DKM5007B4X1` (tests).
- **CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58** — "Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting" — still
  `open` / `plan_complete`; reconcile with this work (the content appears to
  have landed).
- **CG-0MMJ8S8F70FWY2XI** — "Branching & Multi-Level Upgrades" — related
  branching/progression work; potential terminology/UX overlap.
- **CG-0MM8RCLCC0BMV98U** — "Add incident queue state model and engine logic" —
  incident-deck foundation the chains build on.
- **CG-0MLTSPOK705155TZ** — "Refactor common components from games into game
  engine" — relevant if Q3 answers "generalise to core engine".
- **CG-0MU1SJ6D2008WAW2** — "[test-failure] npm test failing" (`open`,
  `plan_complete`) — check whether this touches storyline code.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### OPEN QUESTIONS (awaiting producer)

- **Q1 — Work-item shape / decomposition.** This item bundles three distinct
  deliverables: (a) harden + make flexible the implementation, (b) full
  authoring/management documentation, (c) improvement proposals (tooling +
  player agency). Should it be an **epic** decomposed into children, or one
  feature item?
  - A) **Epic** with children (engine hardening, documentation, tooling
    proposal, player-agency proposal) — *Recommended:* three deliverables with
    different audiences and effort; enables parallel work and independent
    review.
  - B) Single `feature` — implement hardening + docs together; capture
    suggestions later.
  - C) Investigation/design-only (`task`) — produce docs + proposals, no code
    changes.
  - **Status:** OPEN QUESTION — no answer yet (round 1, auto-dispatched
    session).

- **Q2 — Implement the improvement suggestions, or document/propose them?**
  "Suggestions for improvements" could mean deliver design proposals or ship
  the improvements.
  - A) Design doc + prioritised proposals, delivered as **separate work
    items**; implement only the small, low-risk hardening needed to make the
    system consistent and testable — *Recommended:* keeps this item bounded and
    lets the producer schedule improvements deliberately.
  - B) Implement all suggested tooling + player-agency improvements now.
  - C) Implement a producer-prioritised subset now.
  - **Status:** OPEN QUESTION — no answer yet (round 1).

- **Q3 — Generality: Main Street-specific or reusable core-engine module?**
  Should the storyline mechanic be generalised into a reusable core-engine
  module (usable by other games), or stay Main Street-specific with a hardened
  structure?
  - A) Keep it Main Street-specific; harden the data model (validation,
    documented contract, minimal extension seam) — *Recommended:* only one
    consumer exists; avoid premature abstraction (extract when a second game
    needs it).
  - B) Extract a generic core-engine `Storyline` module now.
  - C) Main Street-specific now, but design the model with an explicit
    extraction seam.
  - **Status:** OPEN QUESTION — no answer yet (round 1).

### Answered

- **Q0 — Terminology.** "Storylines" was clarified by repo research to mean the
  Main Street incident event-chain system introduced by
  `CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128` (dual Accept/Reject choices scheduling successor
  incident cards). Evidence: only storyline-like implementation in the repo is
  the `hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId` model, its tests
  (`tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts`) and the `event-choice` transcript
  event. Source: repo research (no interactive reply needed).

- **Q0b — Documentation target location/audience.** Assumed
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` for developers + content designers, with a
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` cross-reference. Source: repo convention
  (`docs/main-street/*` per-subsystem docs; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` index).

data.comment: intake: drafted a provisional brief from repo research (stage left at `idea`). Full draft is now in the work-item description and at `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-write-storylines-CG-0MUB0GFY00001ASV.md`. Summary of findings: 'storylines' = the Main Street dual-choice incident event-chain system from CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128 (fields `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` in `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` + `card-data.csv`; resolution in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`; dialog in `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`; AI in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`). 7 choice cards + 4 terminal escalation cards currently ship. Observed gaps: no documentation, no static chain validation (dangling links only logged at runtime), no authoring/visualisation tooling, binary-only branching, no storyline identity/history/journal, and the content child CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58 is still `open`/`plan_complete`. Three questions (Q1 shape, Q2 implement-vs-propose, Q3 generality) block finalising the brief — see preceding comments. Marked as needing producer review.
